doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

title: Playing Santa at the Stanley Theater in Utica
summary: Ricker recalls playing Santa and conducting the Utica Symphony, and playing the same stage with Mangione when his future wife played oboe.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: This might test your memory a little bit. You know the Stanley Theater in Utica?
Well I have an inside source that said you once played Santa at the Stanley Theater in Utica.
I did. Yes. The clarinet playing Santa.

Yeah another Lego piece. And not only that, once I conducted the Utica Symphony there. And I think it was a holiday concert. It was, it was a holiday concert. I guess they liked me so much as Santa they —
You didn’t know you were auditioning.

No. But what’s really interesting is I played that same place, it wasn’t renovated at the time, but I played at the Stanley Theater with Chuck Mangione and it must have been with the Utica Symphony. But a whole bunch of us went down and played. And my wife was playing second oboe at the time. She was in high school. And she ended up being my wife. And so we didn’t know but we were on the same stage in whenever it was, 1971, I don’t know.
